name: es32-float-targets-and-indexed-blend
title: Float render targets and indexed blending
summary: The seven color-renderable floating-point formats of ES 3.2 (R16F, RG16F, RGBA16F, R32F, RG32F, RGBA32F, R11F_G11F_B10F) hold HDR values (65504, 2^100, 3.75, -2.5) that read back exactly with glReadPixels(RGBA, FLOAT), blend without clamping (32-bit targets only with EXT_float_blend, computed from the extension list), and show an HDR 3D scene (additive glow halos, point lights above 1.0) next to its 8-bit clipped version and a Reinhard tone-mapped one. A 4-attachment MRT framebuffer (RGBA8, RGBA16F, R11F_G11F_B10F, RGBA16F) is drawn under ten per-draw-buffer blend scenarios (glEnablei/glDisablei, glBlendFunci/Separatei, glBlendEquationi/Separatei, glColorMaski, constant color clamping, buffers without alpha); every pixel of every buffer is compared with a CPU model of Tables 15.1/15.2, all indexed state is read back with glIsEnabledi/glGetIntegeri_v/glGetBooleani_v, the non-indexed commands are shown to reset all buffers, and every index >= MAX_DRAW_BUFFERS raises INVALID_VALUE.
spec: ES 3.2 Table 8.10 (sized internal color formats: CR color-renderable, TF texture-filterable, Req. rend.), §9.4 Framebuffer Completeness (§9.4.1 attachment completeness: color attachment needs a color-renderable format, §9.4.2 whole-framebuffer completeness, §9.4.3 Required Framebuffer Formats)

ES 3.2 §9.2.3 Framebuffer Object Queries (FRAMEBUFFER_ATTACHMENT_COMPONENT_TYPE / COLOR_ENCODING / *_SIZE), §9.2.4 Renderbuffer Objects (INVALID_ENUM for a format that is not renderable), §9.2.5 Required Renderbuffer Formats

ES 3.2 §2.3.4.2 16-Bit Floating-Point Numbers, §2.3.4.3 Unsigned 11-Bit Floating-Point Numbers, §2.3.4.4 Unsigned 10-Bit Floating-Point Numbers (negative values convert to zero, values above 65024 / 64512 to the maximum)

ES 3.2 §15.1.5 Blending (no clamping for floating-point color buffers; Enablei/Disablei; INVALID_OPERATION for blending with a 32-bit float draw buffer), §15.1.5.1 Blend Equation (Table 15.1, BlendEquationi), §15.1.5.2 Blend Functions (Table 15.2, BlendFunci), §15.1.5.4 Blend Color, §15.1.5.5 Blending State (initial values, IsEnabledi, GetIntegeri_v, buffer zero for the non-indexed queries; Ad = 1 without an alpha channel), §15.1.6 sRGB Conversion (fixed-point results are clamped to [0, 1])

ES 3.2 §15.2.1 Selecting Buffers for Writing (glDrawBuffers, draw buffer i is COLOR_ATTACHMENTi or NONE), §15.2.2 Fine Control of Buffer Updates (ColorMask, ColorMaski, COLOR_WRITEMASK via GetBooleani_v), §15.2.3 Clearing the Buffers (glClearBufferfv on float buffers)

ES 3.2 §16.1.2 ReadPixels (RGBA / FLOAT for floating-point surfaces, IMPLEMENTATION_COLOR_READ_FORMAT / TYPE), §16.1.3 Obtaining Pixels from the Framebuffer (INVALID_OPERATION for a non-float type from a float buffer; missing G, B, A read as 0, 0, 1)
ES 3.2 §20.1 Simple Queries (GetIntegeri_v / GetBooleani_v errors), §20.2 (IsEnabledi: INVALID_ENUM for state that is not indexed)

GLSL ES 3.20 §3.3 Version, §4.4.2 Output Layout Qualifiers (layout(location) outputs), §4.7 Precision and Precision Qualifiers, §7.1 Built-In Variables (gl_VertexID, gl_FragCoord), §8.9 Texture Functions (texelFetch, textureSize)

api.glEnablei: BLEND on indices 0..3 of the MRT framebuffer and on all MAX_DRAW_BUFFERS indices (junk states): each buffer's pixels follow its own enable flag, IsEnabledi/glGetIntegeri_v read back; INVALID_VALUE for MAX_DRAW_BUFFERS and 0xFFFFFFFF
api.glDisablei: BLEND disabled on single buffers while the others blend (scenarios 0, 1, 4, 7 pixel-compared; a disabled buffer keeps its functions and ignores them); INVALID_VALUE for index = MAX_DRAW_BUFFERS
api.glIsEnabledi: false initially for every index, then equal to the commands issued for all indices after every scenario; INVALID_VALUE for MAX_DRAW_BUFFERS; INVALID_ENUM for DEPTH_TEST
api.glBlendFunci: ONE/ONE, SRC_ALPHA/ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA, SRC_COLOR/DST_COLOR, DST_COLOR/ZERO, ONE_MINUS_DST_ALPHA/DST_ALPHA, ... on single buffers: results of all four buffers match the CPU model of Table 15.2 pixel by pixel, state read back per index; INVALID_VALUE for MAX_DRAW_BUFFERS
api.glBlendFuncSeparatei: four independent factors (SRC_ALPHA, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA, ONE, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA and DST_COLOR, ZERO, ZERO, SRC_ALPHA) change RGB and alpha results separately; read back with BLEND_SRC_RGB/ALPHA, BLEND_DST_RGB/ALPHA per index; INVALID_VALUE for MAX_DRAW_BUFFERS
api.glBlendEquationi: MIN, MAX, FUNC_SUBTRACT, FUNC_REVERSE_SUBTRACT per buffer (MIN ignores the factors), pixel-compared and read back with BLEND_EQUATION_RGB/ALPHA; INVALID_VALUE for MAX_DRAW_BUFFERS
api.glBlendEquationSeparatei: (REVERSE_SUBTRACT, MAX), (MAX, MIN), (FUNC_SUBTRACT, MAX): RGB and alpha follow different equations, pixel-compared and read back; INVALID_VALUE for MAX_DRAW_BUFFERS
api.glColorMaski: different masks on the four buffers with blending off and on: masked components keep their old value (pixel-compared), COLOR_WRITEMASK read back per index; INVALID_VALUE for MAX_DRAW_BUFFERS. The mask TFTT on every buffer with blending enabled is a known deviation on zink (blends the masked channel)
api.glGetIntegeri_v: BLEND_SRC_RGB/DST_RGB/SRC_ALPHA/DST_ALPHA/EQUATION_RGB/EQUATION_ALPHA for all MAX_DRAW_BUFFERS indices initially, after every scenario, after global commands and after rejected commands; INVALID_VALUE for MAX_DRAW_BUFFERS; INVALID_ENUM for DEPTH_FUNC (not indexed)
api.glGetBooleani_v: COLOR_WRITEMASK of all indices (initially TTTT, per-buffer masks, reset by glColorMask); INVALID_VALUE for MAX_DRAW_BUFFERS
api.glEnable: BLEND for all buffers at once: every index reads back enabled while the other state fields of each buffer stay as they were; DEPTH_TEST for the scene
api.glDisable: BLEND for all buffers at once (all indices disabled, the rest untouched); DEPTH_TEST after the scene
api.glIsEnabled: BLEND initially FALSE; reports draw buffer zero (not buffer 1) when buffer zero is disabled; TRUE when buffer zero is enabled and buffer 1 is not (XFAIL on radeonsi: TRUE only when all buffers are enabled)
api.glBlendFunc: sets source/destination factors of all draw buffers (DST_COLOR/ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA, SRC_ALPHA/ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA, SRC_ALPHA_SATURATE/ONE_MINUS_DST_ALPHA, ONE/ONE): all indices read back, the other fields of each buffer unchanged; reset of every index after per-buffer junk; pixels of the float scene (additive glow) and of the accumulation tests
api.glBlendFuncSeparate: four factors for all buffers, read back for all indices (SRC_ALPHA, ONE, DST_ALPHA, ONE_MINUS_DST_COLOR); CONSTANT_COLOR/ONE_MINUS_CONSTANT_COLOR/CONSTANT_ALPHA/ONE_MINUS_CONSTANT_ALPHA pixel-compared on all four buffers
api.glBlendEquation: MAX and REVERSE_SUBTRACT for all buffers: all indices read back, results pixel-compared
api.glBlendEquationSeparate: (FUNC_SUBTRACT, MIN) and (FUNC_ADD, FUNC_ADD) for all buffers: all indices read back, results pixel-compared
api.glBlendColor: (0.5, 2.0, -0.25, 0.75): clamped to [0,1] for the RGBA8 buffer (factor 1.0 for green), unclamped for the float buffers (factor 2.0 and -1.0), pixel-compared; initial (0,0,0,0) read back with glGetFloatv
api.glColorMask: (F,T,F,T) on all buffers and the reset to TTTT: COLOR_WRITEMASK read back for all indices, the other fields untouched; a mask TFTT on all four buffers (XFAIL on zink)
api.glGetBooleanv: COLOR_WRITEMASK reports draw buffer zero (T,F,T,F), not buffer 1
api.glGetIntegerv: MAX_DRAW_BUFFERS (8 here, >= 4), MAX_COLOR_ATTACHMENTS, BLEND_SRC_RGB initially ONE, BLEND_* of draw buffer zero equal buffer zero's indexed values, IMPLEMENTATION_COLOR_READ_TYPE/FORMAT of all seven float formats (type FLOAT, HALF_FLOAT or UNSIGNED_INT_10F_11F_11F_REV)
api.glReadPixels: RGBA/FLOAT of the 16x16 pattern of all seven float formats equal to the CPU model (every texel; 65504, -65504, 2^100, 1000000.5, 3.75, -2.5, 65024 ...), of the RGBA16F scene target, of the RGBA16F/R11F_G11F_B10F MRT attachments; RGBA/UNSIGNED_BYTE of RGBA8 attachments and the window; INVALID_OPERATION for RGBA/UNSIGNED_BYTE from an RGBA16F buffer
api.glReadBuffer: COLOR_ATTACHMENT0..3 select the attachment read back (four different formats of one framebuffer)
api.glClearBufferfv: (3.75, -2.5, 0.5, 2.0) into float renderbuffers and (1, 2, 0.5, 0.5) into float textures: read back exactly, negative values become 0 in R11F_G11F_B10F, missing components 0/0/1
api.glClearColor: HDR target clear value (0.015, 0.02, 0.035): background probes of the scene equal it within half-float precision
api.glClear: COLOR and DEPTH of the HDR scene target (background probes, depth-tested scene probes)
api.glClearDepthf: 1.0 before the scene is drawn; the depth-tested scene (boxes in front of the floor and halos) matches the CPU ray tracer at 122 probe pixels
api.glDrawBuffers: COLOR_ATTACHMENT0..3 of the MRT framebuffer: four fragment outputs reach their own attachments (every pixel of every attachment compared)
api.glDrawArrays: TRIANGLE_STRIP quads from gl_VertexID (pattern, blending, glow, composition) and TRIANGLES (floor, boxes, spheres); INVALID_OPERATION for blending into a 32-bit float buffer is the branch taken when GL_EXT_float_blend is absent (not reached here, all drivers have the extension)
api.glViewport: pattern targets (16x16), HDR target (256x160), MRT quadrants (32x32 at four offsets) and window regions: each region's pixels checked
api.glDepthFunc: LESS for the scene and the glow halos (halo visible only in front of the surface)
api.glDepthMask: FALSE while the additive halos are drawn
api.glGenTextures: pattern targets, RGBA8 control, HDR color, four MRT attachments, not-renderable format probes
api.glBindTexture: TEXTURE_2D targets and the composition samplers
api.glActiveTexture: unit 0 for the compose pass (texelFetch of float textures, results compared in the window)
api.glTexStorage2D: R16F, RG16F, RGBA16F, R32F, RG32F, RGBA32F, R11F_G11F_B10F, RGBA8, RGB32F, RGB9_E5, RGB16F immutable storage; the seven float formats complete as color attachments and carry the pattern
api.glTexParameteri: NEAREST min/mag filters through the typed overloads (R32F is not filterable, default MIN_FILTER would make the textures incomplete)
api.glGenFramebuffers: seven pattern framebuffers, RGBA8 control, HDR scene, MRT, scratch framebuffers
api.glBindFramebuffer: FRAMEBUFFER and READ_FRAMEBUFFER targets; draw buffer and read buffer state are per framebuffer
api.glFramebufferTexture2D: float textures at COLOR_ATTACHMENT0 (complete); RGB32F and RGB9_E5 textures (not color-renderable)
api.glFramebufferRenderbuffer: float renderbuffers at COLOR_ATTACHMENT0 (complete) and DEPTH_COMPONENT24 depth of the HDR target
api.glCheckFramebufferStatus: COMPLETE for all seven float formats as texture and renderbuffer, the RGBA16F + depth framebuffer and the 4-attachment MRT framebuffer; RGB9_E5 gives INCOMPLETE_ATTACHMENT, RGB32F gives UNSUPPORTED on Mesa where INCOMPLETE_ATTACHMENT is required (XFAIL)
api.glGetFramebufferAttachmentParameteriv: COMPONENT_TYPE = FLOAT, COLOR_ENCODING = LINEAR and RED/GREEN/BLUE/ALPHA_SIZE >= Table 8.10 bits (absent components 0) for all seven formats
api.glGenRenderbuffers: seven float renderbuffers, depth renderbuffer, probes for not-renderable formats
api.glRenderbufferStorage: the seven float formats are accepted (storage, completeness, sizes, clear + read back); INVALID_ENUM for RGB32F and RGB9_E5; DEPTH_COMPONENT24
api.glGetRenderbufferParameteriv: RENDERBUFFER_RED/GREEN/BLUE/ALPHA_SIZE >= Table 8.10 bits for the seven float formats (absent components 0)
api.glGenBuffers: vertex buffer of the scene (floor, boxes, spheres)
api.glBufferData: 6 + 3 x 36 + 2 x 1440 vertices of position and normal; probes on lit surfaces equal the CPU ray tracer
api.glBindVertexArray: scene VAO for the geometry; VAO 0 for gl_VertexID quads
api.glVertexAttribPointer: interleaved vec3 position + vec3 normal; lighting probes depend on both
api.glUseProgram: pattern, outputs (4 fragment outputs), scene, glow and compose programs
api.glGetUniformLocation: all uniforms located (an inactive uniform throws); effects visible in the compared pixels
api.glUniform2i: u_origin, u_size of the compose regions; window pixels equal the CPU model
api.glUniform3f: albedo, emission, ambient, sun, halo color and camera vectors: scene probes equal the CPU ray tracer
api.glUniform4fv: u_probe0/u_probe1 (range extremes of the float formats) and u_src[4] (the four fragment colors)
api.glUniformMatrix4fv: view-projection matrix of the scene and halos: probe pixels match the CPU-projected geometry

visual_review.notes: 256x256 captures of radeonsi, llvmpipe and zink viewed; they look identical. Top 160 rows: a perspective 3D scene on a checkered floor with an orange, a blue and a green box and two emissive spheres. Left of the thin grey double line (x = 127/128): the 8-bit view, where the two lamps and their glow halos clip to flat white / pale yellow and the floor next to them loses its gradient; right of it: the same HDR values tone-mapped, where the lamps keep a cyan and white core with soft halos, the boxes keep their lit gradients and the floor falls off smoothly. Middle strip (32 rows): seven 36 x 32 swatches of the float-format pattern textures, vertical stripes of the R ladder (alternating rows green/purple for the sign), R and RG formats show only red/green, RGBA formats all channels, the packed format shows the negative rows as grey (clamped to 0). Bottom 64 rows: four 64 x 64 MRT panels, each split in four colored quadrants: the RGBA8 panel is saturated (clamped, replace), the three float panels show different colors for the same draw (additive, alpha-over with an alpha above 1, reverse subtract), the R11F panel has no negative values. No stray fragments, no unexpected black or magenta. Window-size review (claude-opus-5.5): gpu captures at 333x777 and 1000x200 viewed. The composition now fills the window: the HDR scene is rendered at the size of the top 5/8 (333x486 and 1000x125) with the split line in the middle, clipped lamp and halo on the left, tone-mapped on the right; the seven swatches and the four MRT panels are scaled to the width (swatch row 1/8, MRT row 1/4 of the height), showing the same stripes and quadrant colors as at 256x256.
